text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Monday's Malaysian newspapers.
- Rescuers recover four more bodies from landslide, bringing the death toll in Thursday's disaster to 26.
- Primary Industries Minister Lim Keng Yaik urges palm oil companies to invest in Third World countries as a solution to land and manpower shortages faced by the country.
- Leaner drivers who use small cars for the test will find that they have to park in smaller lots under new regulations to be implemented from September 15.
- Seven more bodies were found, bringing the number of bodies recovered from the aborigine settlement landslide tragedy to 28.

- Trade and business ties between Britain and Malaysia are set for a very busy year ahead due to improved relations, according to Brendan Doyle, the Overseas Trade Services head of Southeast Asia Section of London's Department of Trade and Industry.
- New Tenaga Nasional executive chairman Ahmad Tajuddin Ali has as his top priority the restoration of confidence of the government and the people in the company.
